title: Toscani-Fourier Distance on Probability Measures: Wasserstein Control, Topological Equivalence on Model Classes, and Duality
abstract: arXiv:2609.23163v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Comparing probability measures in machine learning trades transport geometry against computational cost: Wasserstein distances encode the geometry of $\mathbb R^d$ but require solving a transport problem, while kernel discrepancies are cheap to evaluate yet depend delicately on their test class. We study the Toscani--Fourier family $\mathrm T_{s,p}$, the weighted $L^p$ norm of the difference of two characteristic functions, as a continuous Fourier-side discrepancy on $\mathbb R^d$. For $1\le p<\infty$ we show that $d/p<1+d/p$ is exactly the window in which $\mathrm T_{s,p}$ is finite on $\mathcal P_p(\mathbb R^d)$, both endpoints already failing for a pair of Dirac measures, and we establish the metric, embedding, and compactness structure of the resulting space, which we prove to be complete. translated_title: 概率测度上的Toscani-Fourier距离：Wasserstein控制、模型类上的拓扑等价性与对偶性
translated_abstract: 在机器学习中比较概率测度时，需要在传输几何与计算成本之间进行权衡：Wasserstein距离编码了 $\mathbb R^d$ 的几何结构，但需要求解一个传输问题；而核差异（kernel discrepancy）计算代价低廉，却对其测试函数类有着微妙的依赖。我们研究Toscani--Fourier距离族 $\mathrm T_{s,p}$，即两个特征函数之差的加权 $L^p$ 范数，将其作为 $\mathbb R^d$ 上一种连续的“傅里叶侧”差异度量。对于 $1\le p<\infty$，我们证明 $d/p<1+d/p$ 恰好是使 $\mathrm T_{s,p}$ 在 $\mathcal P_p(\mathbb R^d)$ 上有限的参数窗口，且在两个端点处即使对于一对Dirac测度该性质也已失效；我们建立了所得空间的度量、嵌入与紧性结构，并证明该空间是完备的。对偶性将 $\mathrm T_{s,p}$ 刻画为齐次傅里叶--Lebesgue球上的积分概率度量，并给出了显式的极值函数……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将Toscani-Fourier距离 $\mathrm T_{s,p}$ 确立为Wasserstein距离的低计算成本替代方案，精确刻画了其在 $\mathcal P_p(\mathbb R^d)$ 上的有限性窗口与完备度量结构，并证明其对Wasserstein距离的控制能力、在模型类上的拓扑等价性以及作为积分概率度量的对偶表示。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes the Toscani-Fourier distance T_{s,p} as a computationally cheap Fourier-side alternative to Wasserstein distances, precisely characterizes its finiteness window and complete metric structure on P_p(R^d), and proves its control of the Wasserstein distance, topological equivalence on model classes, and a dual representation as an integral probability metric.
